correctness.rationale: For hub-free sets maximality forces the entire rim. With hub, the cycle excess equals the number of selected rim edges; adding a missing vertex gives exact zero-edge alternating or unique-11 and short-zero-gap classifications. The n-fold start count is unique, and the binomial, rational, spectrum and asymptotic deductions follow. A separate graph component enumeration through n=16 and a rational-coefficient recurrence through n=180 concur. The n=3 boundary is included.

evidence: Existing theorems give parameterized algorithms and kernels for general-graph pseudoforest deletion.
A bicircular-matroid pseudoforest uses edge-subset independence and differs from a vertex-induced subset maximal under adding a vertex.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General-graph decision and optimization algorithms are not stronger enumeration theorems; no derivation of the labelled wheel distribution from their stated claims was found. Edge-maximal bases do not encode vertex-induced maximality.

evidence: The 2020 algorithm determines fixed-parameter decision complexity for pseudoforest deletion.
The 2015/2018 algorithm gives fixed-parameter algorithms and polynomial kernels for generalized pseudoforest deletion.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither a deletion decision algorithm nor a kernel-size theorem implies the explicit counts of every inclusion-minimal wheel solution, its gapped cardinality support, or the rational generating function. The new claim is a distinct graph-family enumeration.

evidence: The 2020 paper defines pseudoforest deletion by at most one cycle per component.
The 2015/2018 generalized pseudoforest deletion paper defines the same hereditary graph property and constructs decision algorithms and kernels.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The complement of an inclusion-maximal induced pseudoforest is an inclusion-minimal vertex deletion set, so both formulations were compared. The inspected algorithmic results address feasibility or minimum size, not all inclusion-minimal wheel solutions or their labelled size distribution.

evidence: The inspected introductions and theorem statements give algorithms and complexity results rather than wheel-specific coefficient tables.
The cyclic-run coefficients are directly reproducible from the embedded verifier for small orders.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: No cited table provides the complete all-order, cardinality-refined wheel enumeration. Available indices and primary-text checks cannot exclude all unindexed enumerations.

originality.rationale: The available closest primary works concern parameterized algorithms or kernels for pseudoforest vertex deletion. Searches for wheel all-size enumeration, minimal deletion-set spectra, induced pseudoforest and equivalent binary-run restrictions in scholarly and research records did not identify equivalent claim. The theorem is not a corollary of the cited decision or kernel-size guarantees. Provisional priority remains subject to unindexed or uninspected sources.
residual_risks: Unindexed work or an uninspected part of a broad paper could contain an equivalent exact wheel enumeration.
No independent mathematical literature audit has been conducted.

value.rationale: The exact labelled polynomial enumerates all inclusion-minimal pseudoforest vertex-deletion solutions in a canonical infinite connected planar family. The sharp noninterval support has a forbidden interval of growing length, distinguishing minimum-size optimization from inclusion-minimal solution structure. Rationality, extremal multiplicities, and the plastic-constant growth rate provide further useful exact invariants.
